card.name: Verb or negation before an adjective
card.fires_on: A subject noun or a form of "be" or "not" in general web prose, right where a predicate adjective or participle is expected next (e.g. "is not satisfied", "will not be complicit").

modes.label: Be-verb or not
modes.description: The word "be", "are", "was" or "not" comes just before a descriptive adjective.
modes.example: This sends a clear message that we will not<< be>> complicit in the settlement programme.

modes.label: Subject noun
modes.description: A noun like "company" or "households" ends a subject phrase that is followed by a verb or description.
modes.example: So far, however, Gilead is the only Western<< company>> to join.

card.writes: The promoted words are forms of "prepared", so it makes a predicate like "be prepared" or "are prepared" more likely next.
card.plain: It fires where a sentence is about to say that someone is or is not in some state, such as prepared or willing.
